title: 1000만 고지 오른 알뜰폰… ‘싼 맛’ 다음 경쟁 시작
partialText: 서울 서대문구에 위치한 알뜰폰 스퀘어. (제공: 한국알뜰통신사업자협회) [천지일보=손고은 기자] 10년 가까이 이어진 알뜰폰(MVNO) 성장의 원동력은 가격이었다. 더 싸고 단순한 요금제가 소비자를 움직였고 그 결과 알뜰폰 가입자는 1000만 회선을 넘어섰다. 성공 이후 새로운 숙제가 생겼다. 더 낮은 가격으로 고객을 끌어오는 전략은 한계에 다다르고 있다. 월 10원 요금제까지 등장한 시장에서 가격 인하만으로 새로운 고객을 끌어오는 시대는 저물고 있다. ◆성장 신화 이후의 숙제 알뜰폰 시장은 올해 1000만 가입자를 돌파하며 국내 이동통신 시장의 한 축으로 자리 잡았다. 한때 이동통신 3사의 높은 요금제에 대한 대안으로 출발한 알뜰폰은 저렴한 LTE 요금제와 공격적인 프로모션을 앞세워 빠르게 성장했다. 다만 성장 곡선은 둔화하고 있다. 13일 한국통신사업자연합회(KTOA)에 따르면 알뜰폰 번호이동 시장은 올해 1~3월 순증 폭이 점차 줄어든 뒤 4월과 5월 두 달 연속 순감으로 전환됐다. 이에 대한 해석은 엇갈린다. 일각에서는 이를 통신 3사의 저가 통합요금제 확대 영향으로 해석하지만 알뜰폰 시장 전체가 직접적인 타격을 받는 것은 아니라는 분석도 나온다. 월 10원대부터 5000원 안팎 초저가 요금제는 여전히 알뜰폰의 핵심 경쟁 영역이다. 통신 3사의 2만~3만원대 통합요금제와 경쟁하는 구간은 데이터 제공량과 혜택을 강화한 일부 중·고가 알뜰폰 상품군에 가깝다. 한국알뜰통신사업자협회는 정부의 통신비 인하 정책이 이동통신 3사의 요금 인하에 집중되는 점을 우려하고 있다. 스마텔 대표 고명수 한국알뜰통신사업자협회장은 “통신비 인하 정책이 통신 3사의 요금 인하에만 집중될 경우 알뜰폰의 경쟁 기반이 약화될 수 있다”며 “도매대가를 낮추고 전파사용료를 30~40% 감면해 알뜰폰 시장의 자체 경쟁력을 강화할 수 있도록 해야 한다”고 피력했다. ◆‘더 싸게’ 말고 ‘다르게’​ 가격 중심 경쟁의 한계가 드러나면서 알뜰폰 사업자들은 금융·유통·콘텐츠 결합 등 비가격 전략을 통한 차별화에 나서고 있다. 대표적으로 금융권 알뜰폰은 통신을 단순한 요금 상품이 아닌 금융 생태계 확장의 접점으로 활용하는 방식이다. KB국민은행의 알뜰폰 ‘리브모바일’​과 우리은행의 ‘우리WON모바일’​은 단순히 통신요금만 낮추는 데 집중하지 않는다. 통신 가입자를 금융 서비스 이용 고객으로 전환하는 게 목적이다. 리브모바일은 통신비 납부 데이터를 대출 심사 시 연체 가능성 판단 지표로 활용하는 등 금융 데이터와의 연계에 초점을 맞추고 있다. 우리WON모바일은 금융거래 실적에 따라 통신요금을 할인해주고 우리카드와 연계한 혜택을 제공한다. 프로모션 기간에는 할인 폭을 확대하는 방식으로 가입 유인을 강화한다. 이 같은 전략으로 출시 1년 만에 소비자 만족도 1위를 기록했다. 가격을 넘어선 또 다른 변화 축은 유통망 확대다. 그동안 알뜰폰은 온라인 셀프 개통 중심으로 성장해왔다. 하지만 가입자 1000만 시대를 맞아 기존 통신 상품에 익숙하지 않거나 대면 상담을 선호하는 소비자를 겨냥한 오프라인 전략의 중요성도 커지고 있다. 편의점과 대형마트를 중심으로 알뜰폰 오프라인 접점 확대가 이어지고 있다. SK텔링크는 이마트24 5500여 매장에 공용 유심 ‘간편유심’을 출시해 소비자가 현장에서 유심 구매 후 즉시 개통할 수 있도록 했다. LG유플러스는 이마트에 ‘알뜰폰플러스’ 매장을 열고 상담·개통·고객 서비스까지 제공하는 오프라인 창구를 전국 9개 지점에서 운영 중이다. ◆정부 지원책 윤곽 속 업계는 ‘실효성’에 주목 알뜰폰 시장 경쟁 구도가 변화하는 가운데 정부도 제도 정비에 나선다. 정부는 올해 중 ‘알뜰폰 생태계 활성화 혁신 방안’을 발표하고 시행할 계획이다. 업계에서는 구체적인 내용에 주목하면서도 “실질적인 반영이 이뤄져야 한다”는 목소리가 나온다. 업계가 가장 강하게 요구하는 것은 비용 구조 개선이다. 도매대가 인하와 전파사용료 30~40% 감면 등을 통해 알뜰폰 시장의 경쟁력을 강화해야 한다는 입장이다. 올해부터 알뜰폰 사업자들은 전파사용료의 50%를 부담해야 하고 내년에는 전액을 내야 한다. 정부가 도매대가 산정에서 손을 뗀 이후 SK텔레콤이 가격 협상 주도권을 쥐게 된 것도 중소 사업자에게는 부담이다. 제도 설계 측면에서는 풀 MVNO 진입장벽 완화가 핵심 과제로 꼽힌다. 풀 MVNO는 무선망을 제외한 가입자 관리·요금 청구·SIM 발급 등 통신 인프라를 자체 구축·운영하는 사업자를 말한다. 자생력을 갖춘 사업자를 키운다는 취지지만 국내에서는 막대한 투자 비용과 명확한 기준 부재로 성공 사례가 없다. 업계는 사업 규모와 역할에 따라 다양한 유형의 MVNO를 인정하고 단계적으로 성장할 수 있는 제도 설계가 필요하다는 입장이다. 요금제 설계나 빌링 시스템 등 일부 핵심 기능만 자체 운영하고 나머지 인프라는 기존 통신사나 풀 MVNO로부터 지원받는 중간 단계 사업자 모델을 허용해야 한다는 제언도 나온다. 일본 사례는 해당 모델의 실현 가능성을 보여주는 참고 사례로 평가된다. 일본에서는 슈퍼마켓이나 세탁소 같은 소규모 사업자도 MVNO 사업에 참여할 수 있다. 직접 통신 설비를 구축하지 않아도 기존 인프라를 활용해 시장에 진입할 수 있는 구조다. 지역 밀착형 MVNO가 활성화된 배경이기도 하다. 고 협회장은 “말만 듣고 끝나는 요식행위가 아닌 실질적인 반영을 통해 업계에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있는 제도가 나오길 기대한다”고 말했다.

title: BNK경남은행, 먹깨비 배달서비스 오픈
partialText: 공공배달앱 서비스 오픈. (제공: 경남은행)ⓒ천지일보 2026.06.13. [천지일보 경남=이선미 기자] BNK경남은행이 고객과 지역 소상공인들이 함께 혜택을 누릴 수 있는 공공배달앱 서비스를 선보였다. 경남은행은 공공배달앱 운영사 먹깨비와 협약을 맺고 모바일뱅킹앱(App)에 먹깨비 배달주문 서비스를 오픈했다고 밝혔다. 먹깨비 배달주문 서비스는 민간 배달앱보다 가맹점 수수료 부담을 낮추고 제로페이·쿠폰 혜택을 연계해 지역 소상공인과 고객을 함께 지원하는 플랫폼이다. BNK경남은행은 모바일뱅킹앱 내 공공배달 전용 채널을 구축해 가맹점 등록부터 주문·결제까지 한 번에 처리할 수 있도록 했다. 이용자는 모바일뱅킹앱 생활혜택 코너에서 '먹깨비 배달 주문하기'를 클릭한 뒤 원하는 음식점의 메뉴를 주문·결제하면 된다. 서비스 오픈을 기념해 BNK경남은행 모바일뱅킹앱으로 먹깨비 첫 주문 시 할인 혜택을 제공하고 있다. 향후 포인트 페이백 혜택도 지급할 예정이다. 이주형 AI/디지털그룹 부행장은 “먹깨비 배달주문 서비스가 지역 소상공인들이 안정적인 매출 기반을 마련하는 데 도움이 되고 고객들에게 각종 혜택을 제공하는 좋은 기회가 되길 바란다”며 “지역 경제 활성화와 생활 편의 증진을 위해 다양한 제휴 서비스를 지속적으로 확대해 나가겠다”고 말했다. 한편 BNK경남은행은 지역 소상공인 지원을 위해 먹깨비 소상공인 입점 서비스도 운영하고 있다. 먹깨비 가맹점에 입점한 소상공인에게는 3만원 상당의 상품권과 일회용 앞치마, 젓가락 등으로 구성된 웰컴키트 패키지를 제공한다. 먹깨비는 지난해 9월 경상남도가 주관하는 공공배달앱 운영사로 선정됐다. 같은 해 12월 공공배달앱 활성화를 위해 BNK경남은행·김해시와 업무협약을 체결한 바 있다.

title: 혜택은 돌아왔지만 통신은 떠나고 있다 [IT 판 읽기]
partialText: 이동통신 3사 로고. (제공: 각 사) ⓒ천지일보 2022.09.12 [천지일보=손고은 기자] 통신사들이 갑자기 고객에게 친절해졌다. 장기 고객 혜택을 강화하고 Z세대 맞춤 마케팅을 확대하며 구독 서비스까지 앞세운다. 불과 몇 년 전만 해도 비용 효율화에 무게를 두던 통신사들의 방향이 바뀌었다. 해킹 사태와 정책 변화로 시장의 균형이 흔들리면서 다시 고객 경쟁의 시대로 들어섰다. ◆“혜택이 왜 이렇게 줄었지” SK텔레콤·KT·LG유플러스는 매년 멤버십 혜택을 조금씩 축소해 왔다. 한 번에 크게 깎는 방식이 아니었다. 제휴 혜택이 슬그머니 조정되고 한때 알짜로 불리던 포인트 항목이 하나씩 사라지는 식이었다. 개별 변경 폭은 크지 않았지만 오랜 기간 누적되면서 일부 소비자들은 과거보다 체감 혜택이 줄었다고 느끼기 시작했다. 별도의 공지 없이 약관 변경 안내 한 줄로 처리되는 경우가 많았다. 소비자 입장에서는 멤버십 혜택 체감은 낮아진 반면 고가 5G 요금제 중심의 마케팅은 강화됐다는 평가가 나왔다. ‘초고속·초저지연·초연결’ 을 내세운 5G 마케팅이 쏟아졌지만 전국 어디서나 5G가 안정적으로 터지지 않는다는 불만은 꾸준히 제기됐다. 지하철 안에서, 건물 안에서 LTE로 떨어지는 일이 반복됐다. 소비자들은 LTE보다 비싼 요금을 내면서도 5G를 온전히 누리지 못한다는 피로감을 쌓아갔다. 통신사들의 마케팅 방향은 바뀌지 않았다. 혜택은 줄이고 더 비싼 요금제로 유도하는 구조가 수년간 이어졌다. 3사 모두 비슷한 흐름이었다. 과열 경쟁보다는 기존 가입자 유지 중심의 시장 구조가 이어졌다. 마케팅 비용 부담도 과거보다 작아졌다. 설비투자(CAPEX)도 마찬가지였다. 5G 초기 구축 이후 망 고도화에 쓰는 돈을 서서히 줄여왔다. 혁신을 내세웠지만 투자 숫자는 해마다 뒷걸음쳤다. ◆균형을 깬 건 해킹… 정책이 판 바꿨다 2025년 SK텔레콤 해킹 사태가 그 균형을 흔들었다. 가입자 정보가 유출되면서 소비자 신뢰가 무너졌고 오랫동안 잠잠하던 번호이동 시장이 움직이기 시작했다. 통신사들은 서둘러 가입자 방어에 나섰고 수년간 이어져온 조용한 균형이 깨졌다. 때마침 ‘이동통신단말장치 유통구조 개선에 관한 법률(단통법)’도 폐지됐다. 오랫동안 묶여 있던 보조금이 풀리면서 시장은 빠르게 달아올랐다. 소비자들이 통신사를 바꾸기 시작하자 3사는 오랜만에 본격적인 가입자 쟁탈전을 벌였다. 이재명 정부 출범 이후 통신 시장을 둘러싼 환경은 더 빠르게 바뀌었다. 기본 통신권 보장 기조 아래 LTE와 5G 요금제 간 장벽이 허물어졌고 데이터를 다 써도 카카오톡 등 기본 통신 기능을 유지할 수 있는 400kbps 속도가 전 요금제에 기본 탑재됐다. 통신은 사실상 보편적 공공재로 규정됐다. 통신사 입장에서는 고가 요금제를 권유할 명분이 줄어들었다. 5G를 더 잘 구축해도 요금 차별화로 이어지기 어려운 구조가 됐다. 수년째 줄이던 멤버십 혜택으로는 더 이상 가입자를 붙잡기 어렵다는 판단도 섰다. 알뜰폰의 저가 공세까지 거세지면서 순수 통신 요금만으로는 성장이 불가능하다는 인식이 업계 안에서 자리를 잡기 시작했다. ◆고객은 붙잡고, 돈은 밖에서 찾는다 통신사들이 선택한 새로운 전략은 구독 서비스였다. SK텔레콤의 ‘T우주’, LG유플러스의 ‘유독’ 같은 플랫폼은 OTT·독서·쇼핑·편의점 혜택을 묶어 제공한다. 1만원대 알뜰폰 요금제에 맞먹는 구독 혜택을 얹어 가격 경쟁 대신 소비자의 일상 고정비를 자사 플랫폼에 묶어두는 전략이다. Z세대 마케팅과 장기고객 우대 프로그램도 같은 맥락이다. 안으로는 구독 경쟁, 밖으로는 B2B 신사업이다. 통신사들은 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 구축, 기업용 AI 솔루션, 자율주행 및 UAM(도심항공교통)을 위한 고정밀 네트워크 등 정부 규제의 직접 타깃이 되지 않는 기업 대상 사업에 투자를 집중하고 있다. 문제는 통신망이다. 3사의 설비투자 규모는 수년째 감소해 6조원대 수준으로 낮아졌다. 고가 요금제로 유도할 인프라적 차별점이 사라진 마당에 통신사들이 6G 연구나 망 고도화에 선뜻 지갑을 열 유인은 갈수록 줄어들고 있다. 통신망은 유지·보수 수준으로만 관리되고 품질 향상은 정체되는 흐름이 이어질 수 있다는 우려가 업계 안팎에서 나온다. 혜택은 돌아왔다. 경쟁도 돌아왔다. 통신은 떠나고 있다. 통신사들은 구독을 팔고, AI 데이터센터를 짓고, 기업 고객을 찾는다. 한 가지 질문만 남는다. 통신사가 통신 밖에서 미래를 찾는 시대, 통신망 투자는 어떤 우선순위를 갖게 될까.

title: [GAFH 2026] Li Haonan: “We Must Focus on AI’s Impact, Not Just Its Capabilities”
partialText: [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Li Haonan, CEO of Ximeng Technology, delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. In his presentation, Li discusses the importance of building trustworthy AI systems and explores strategies for promoting the practical adoption and industrialization of artificial intelligence through transparency, reliability, and responsible innovation. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Kim Nuri] Li Haonan, Founder and CEO of Ximeng AI, emphasized that the most important discussion surrounding artificial intelligence is not about its functions themselves, but about how AI can transform society and create meaningful change. Li made the remarks on June 12 during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. Speaking on the theme “AI Industrial Strategy and Policy for Human Co-Prosperity,” Li noted that some technology experts predict China’s AI industry will experience another major leap forward by around 2030. “What is clear,” he said, “is that AI is moving beyond the stage of large-scale experimentation and entering a phase of widespread practical application.” [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Li Haonan, CEO of Ximeng Technology, delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. The session focuses on the importance of developing reliable and accountable AI systems, as well as strategies for advancing the industrial adoption of artificial intelligence in ways that promote innovation, trust, and sustainable growth. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. He argued that the focus should not be on developing larger models, more advanced features, or more powerful capabilities. “What we should be discussing is not bigger models or stronger functions, but how AI can transform the way people live and work,” Li said. “If AI can be turned into a widely accessible productive tool, communication among people can become more active and effective, creating a foundation for human co-prosperity.” Li explained that the successful implementation of AI depends on effective integration among three layers: technology, industry, and applications. According to him, the concept of human co-prosperity should not be understood as equal distribution or universal equality. “The model we pursue is closer to a diffusion structure,” he said. “The key lies in how we accept and utilize new systems in ways that are applicable to real industrial environments.” [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Li Haonan, CEO of Ximeng Technology, delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization” during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. His presentation highlights the importance of developing trustworthy, transparent, and accountable AI systems while exploring pathways for the effective industrialization and real-world application of artificial intelligence. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. Li also stressed the importance of trust in AI systems. “Without trust, it is impossible to achieve sustainable scalability,” he said. “Without accountability, practical adoption is also impossible. People will inevitably fear that AI may harm them or negatively affect their lives.” He further emphasized the need for human oversight. “There can be no shared development without human control,” he stated. “In this process, we will inevitably face difficult realities, including competition and conflicting interests across different global contexts.” According to Li, transparency and trust should serve as the minimum common standards for global AI governance. “We must consider what policies governments should implement and how to build strong infrastructure and professional expertise,” he said. Li observed that competition in AI is gradually shifting from a technology-centered paradigm toward an intelligence-centered one. “For AI to become widely adopted, we need national development strategies, cross-border technological cooperation, capacity building, and communication,” he said. “The future of AI does not depend solely on technological breakthroughs. It depends on whether we can build trustworthy and sustainable industrial ecosystems.” [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Li Haonan, CEO of Ximeng Technology, speaks during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. Li delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization,” discussing the importance of building reliable AI systems and promoting their responsible adoption across industries to support sustainable innovation and human-centered development. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. During the question-and-answer session, Li was asked how large corporations could support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the AI era. He responded that traditional approaches are insufficient but suggested that government-supported cloud computing platforms and foundation models developed by major corporations could provide valuable support for SMEs. “The ability to train and develop proprietary AI models will have a significant impact on a company’s future competitiveness,” he said. Li noted that China is expected to have more than 100 AI models by 2030, although only a limited number of major AI companies currently dominate the sector. “If SMEs develop successful AI use cases, they can provide new opportunities and solutions for large enterprises,” he explained. “This could become a pathway toward greater cooperation and harmony between small and large businesses.” When asked how countries could establish common values and principles for AI governance, Li acknowledged that complete trust among nations may be unrealistic. “However, there is a clear need to establish a unified global AI framework and shared standards,” he said. “We should develop international AI standards centered on transparency, openness, and safety.” Li concluded that global cooperation on trustworthy AI standards will be essential for ensuring that AI serves humanity's long-term interests and contributes to sustainable development and shared prosperity.

title: [GAFH 2026] Lalit Agarwal: “We Must Bridge the Empathy Divide” — Calls for AI-Powered Peace Education
partialText: [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Lalit Agarwal, Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation of India, delivers a presentation on “Embedding Ethics and Peace” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. In his presentation, Agarwal discusses the importance of integrating ethical principles and peace-oriented values into the development and application of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need for human-centered AI that contributes to social harmony and global well-being. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Hwang Hae-yeon] Lalit Agarwal, Vice Chancellor of the MERI (Management Education & Research Institute) Foundation and a Ph.D. in Philosophy, called for the use of AI-powered peace education to prevent social conflicts and build sustainable peace infrastructure during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026), held on June 12 at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. The MERI Foundation is one of India’s leading multidisciplinary educational institutions, having produced professionals in fields such as business administration, information technology, law, journalism, and engineering for more than three decades. Speaking under the theme “Human-Centered Values: Embedding Ethics and Peace,” Agarwal argued that despite unprecedented levels of digital connectivity and technological advancement, social divisions are becoming increasingly severe. “We are more digitally connected than ever before, yet more socially divided than ever before,” he said. “We have built highways of communication, but we have failed to teach people how to travel those roads without colliding with one another.” He warned that the traditional digital divide has evolved into a far more dangerous phenomenon that he called the “Empathy Divide.” “Why is it that our technological capabilities are advancing exponentially, while our psychological capacities for understanding, communication, and empathy are lagging so far behind?” he asked. Agarwal identified educational inequality, the spread of misinformation, declining social trust, and political and cultural polarization as major risk factors contributing to conflict. He also highlighted the enormous economic costs associated with violence and instability. “According to the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP), the global economic impact of violence reached nearly $20 trillion in 2024,” he said. “That means conflict and violence consume approximately 11.6 percent of global GDP.” To address these challenges, he advocated moving beyond traditional conflict-response models toward AI-enabled preventive peace systems. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Dr. Park Jeong-jin (center), a cultural anthropologist, and Lalit Agarwal (right), Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation of India, answer questions following their presentations at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. The two speakers presented on the theme of “Embedding Ethics and Peace”, highlighting the importance of integrating human-centered values, ethical responsibility, and peace-building principles into the development and governance of artificial intelligence. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. “We propose a fundamental paradigm shift—from reactive conflict prevention to Proactive Peace Learning Systems,” Agarwal said. “Peace is not the result of geographical luck or an easy choice. Peace is a capability that societies must continuously learn.” He described AI as a powerful tool capable of delivering personalized peace education tailored to individuals and communities. “AI can make peace education fully adaptive, context-sensitive, and infinitely scalable,” he explained. At the same time, he stressed three essential principles for the responsible use of AI in peacebuilding: human centricity, respect for cultural context, and the prevention of cognitive offloading. “AI must never become a black box that replaces human beings,” he said. “Its role should be to amplify the capabilities of educators and extend their positive impact.” He also warned against what he called “algorithmic colonialism.” “We must firmly reject the idea that peace models designed in Silicon Valley can simply be copied and applied unchanged in East Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, or Latin America,” he said. Agarwal also introduced the TARP (Total Assessment of Risk and Peace) framework developed by MERI. “If something cannot be measured, it cannot be managed or optimized,” he explained. “TARP is a quantitative framework designed to objectively assess whether an environment is moving toward stability or sliding into conflict.” He further presented the concept of the “Peace Dividend,” arguing that investments in peace education generate significant social and economic returns. “Investing in peace education is not charity,” he said. “It is one of the most effective investment multipliers available to modern economies.” “According to our data, the peacebuilding investment multiplier is 1:16. Every dollar invested can generate sixteen dollars in value through reduced conflict-related costs.” In his concluding remarks, Agarwal emphasized the importance of international cooperation and governance frameworks for building AI-enabled peace infrastructure. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Dr. Park Jeong-jin (center), a cultural anthropologist, and Lalit Agarwal (right), Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation in India, answer questions after delivering presentations on “Embedding Ethics and Peace” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. The session explored the importance of integrating ethical values and peace-oriented principles into the development and governance of artificial intelligence to ensure that AI contributes to human well-being and social harmony. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. “Peace is not merely the absence of war,” he said. “Peace exists when societies possess the infrastructure that makes war unnecessary.” “The infrastructure of 2026 must be digital, educational, and integrated,” he added. “AI can serve as the foundation of that infrastructure.” He encouraged participants to work together to bridge the empathy divide and build learning systems that strengthen communities. During the Q&A session, discussions focused on the economic value of peace education and the feasibility of AI-based peace governance. When asked whether global corporations could prioritize peace education as part of their ESG agendas, Agarwal replied: “Peace enables sustainable market success, resilient supply chains, and lower insurance costs. A war economy benefits only a few, while a peace economy benefits all of humanity.” Responding to concerns that the TARP model could be misused as a surveillance tool, he emphasized that it is designed as a predictive framework for prevention rather than monitoring. “TARP is not a surveillance system,” he said. “It is an indicator framework based on voluntary participation by governments, organizations, and communities.” When questioned about the effectiveness of a governance “kill switch” for AI systems, Agarwal explained that the concept refers not to a physical mechanism but to an internationally agreed oversight structure. He stressed the need for transparency, open-source governance, and review procedures for advanced AI systems. “A multi-stakeholder oversight framework involving diplomats, technology experts, and civil society organizations is entirely feasible,” he said. “It will require further discussion and refinement, but it represents a practical and realistic solution.” The forum was held under the theme “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity” and served as an international platform for exploring how advances in artificial intelligence can be aligned with human-centered values and the shared prosperity of humanity.

title: [GAFH 2026] Sang-myeon Lee: “The Key to AI Development Is Not Technology, but Values and Principles”
partialText: ​[Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Jun-seong Park] Sang-myeon Lee, CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, delivers the opening remarks at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. ⓒCheonji Ilbo 2026.06.12. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Min-hee Kim] “AI must develop in a way that safeguards human dignity and freedom — the universal values of humanity.” Sang-myeon Lee, CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, emphasized the importance of human-centered values behind technological advancement during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026), held on June 12 at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. The forum, themed “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” brought together experts from Korea and abroad to discuss AI reliability, ethics, and international cooperation. As chairman of the organizing committee, Lee said in his opening remarks, “We are living in an era of profound transformation in which artificial intelligence is reshaping not only industry and the economy but also the future course of human civilization.” He noted that AI presents new possibilities for addressing long-standing challenges facing humanity, including medical innovation, narrowing educational gaps, and improving social welfare. At the same time, he warned of the risks associated with the technology, saying AI could accelerate threats such as the spread of misinformation, human alienation, surveillance and control, the production of optimized weapons designed to kill, and even the destruction of civilization. Lee stressed that discussions surrounding AI should focus not only on technological capabilities but also on the values and principles that guide its development. “More important than how advanced AI becomes is the question of what values and principles will shape its future,” he said. He added that ensuring AI serves humanity requires global cooperation and a shared commitment to protecting human dignity, freedom, and universal values. ​[Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Jun-seong Park] Sang-myeon Lee, CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, delivers the opening remarks at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. ⓒCheonji Ilbo 2026.06.12. Lee reiterated that “what matters is not merely the speed of technological advancement,” emphasizing that “AI must develop in a way that safeguards human dignity and freedom — the universal values of humanity.” He also stressed that AI should “contribute to the peace, coexistence, and shared prosperity of all humanity beyond differences in nationality, social class, culture, and ideology,” adding that “the international community should consider AI governance from the perspective of cooperation rather than engaging in a hegemonic race for technological supremacy.” In particular, he stated that “trustworthy AI, human-centered ethics, and responsible innovation are not matters of choice but shared tasks for all of us living in the era beyond humanity.” He added, “We need international solidarity and common principles so that AI develops not in a direction that replaces or controls human beings, but in a way that expands human values and fosters healthier communities.” Lee further expressed hope that “the Joint Declaration of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, to be adopted today, will serve as a meaningful milestone in sharing AI principles and practical directions for human co-prosperity with the international community.” [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Jun-seong Park] Former National Assembly member Sun-dong Kim delivers a congratulatory speech at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. ⓒCheonji Ilbo 2026.06.12. Former National Assembly member Sun-dong Kim, who delivered a congratulatory address, said, “If the Industrial Revolution expanded human power, AI is expanding human thinking, creativity, and problem-solving capabilities.” He added, “As rapidly as technology advances, we must give equally serious thought to the direction in which it is heading.” He continued, “The real question is not how much further we can develop AI, but whether we are prepared for a new era in which humanity and AI coexist.” He emphasized that society must consider “how to protect human dignity and freedom, and on what values and principles AI should operate.” Meanwhile, the forum brought together AI experts, academics, industry leaders, and political figures from Korea and abroad. Participants engaged in presentations and discussions on topics including global AI governance, international cooperation, human-centered values, and the design of trustworthy AI systems.

title: [GAFH 2026] “AI for Peace, Not Weaponization” : 300+ Global Experts and Citizens Sign Landmark AI Governance Declaration at Korea Chamber of Commerce
partialText: [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] Participants pose for a commemorative photo after signing the Joint Declaration of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul on June 12, 2026. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo 2026.06.12. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Yang Hyo-sun] SEOUL, June 12 — Participants at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) adopted a landmark joint declaration Thursday, outlining six principles for trustworthy AI and international cooperation under the vision of “Human Co-Prosperity.” The declaration was announced during GAFH 2026, hosted by South Korea-based newspaper Cheonji Ilbo at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in central Seoul to mark the newspaper’s 17th anniversary. The forum was organized by Cheonji Ilbo, which also produced this report. More than 300 participants from four countries — including Belgium, India, and China — attended the forum, spanning politics, society, media, academia, and industry, as well as international representatives from AI governance bodies and the technology sector. Building on the spirit of “Human Co-Prosperity” first articulated in the 2025 Declaration of the Spirit of the AI Transformation Era, the document seeks to expand the concept to the international level and establish common principles for AI governance in an era of rapid technological transformation. The declaration comes as governments and international organizations around the world intensify efforts to establish common rules for artificial intelligence, including the EU AI Act and ongoing UN discussions. Lee Sang-myeon, chief executive of Cheonji Ilbo and organizing committee chair of the forum, set the tone in his opening remarks. “What matters most in the age of AI is not the technology itself, but the values it is made to serve,” he said. Participants recognized that the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is exerting a profound influence on the future of humanity and the international order. The declaration states that AI is a powerful tool capable of addressing humanity’s shared challenges, including the climate crisis, pandemics, educational inequality, poverty and conflict. At the same time, it warns that without proper control and accountability, AI also poses risks that may threaten human dignity, freedom, democracy and international peace. The six-point declaration identifies Human Co-Prosperity as the guiding principle of the AI era. “The global direction of the AI era must be founded not on the interests of specific groups, but on the Human Co-Prosperity of all humankind,” the declaration states. “Technological advancement should proceed according to the principles of cooperation and responsibility, rather than competition and domination.” The document also emphasizes a human-centered approach to AI development and deployment. “AI must respect human dignity and fundamental rights and be developed and utilized under meaningful human oversight,” it says. “The values of freedom, peace, equality, and respect for life must be embedded throughout the entire AI lifecycle.” On international security, participants declared unequivocally that AI must serve as a tool for peace and cooperation — never for conflict or weaponization — and must never be used in ways that undermine international peace and security. The signatories also called for concerted efforts to minimize inequality and discrimination arising from AI while strengthening international safety standards, transparency and accountability frameworks for high-risk AI systems. Addressing the need for international cooperation, the declaration stresses that the transnational impact of AI requires a broad and inclusive governance framework. “To address the transnational impact of AI, we affirm that inclusive and responsible global governance is essential, involving international organizations, governments, businesses, academia, and civil society,” it states. “The safety and accountability of AI are shared responsibilities of all humankind.” The declaration further calls for the active use of AI in achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), responding to climate change, preventing pandemics, advancing education, eradicating poverty and building peace. Participants reaffirmed that “AI is not a force to replace humanity, but a collaborative partner that expands human capability and responsibility.” They also declared that the agreement reached at GAFH 2026 “will become an important milestone in the development of international AI governance,” pledging to continue their shared responsibility and solidarity for the future of human co-prosperity. During the forum’s final session, Song Tae-bok — managing director and editor-in-chief of Cheonji Ilbo and secretary-general of the forum — formally read the declaration aloud before the full assembly. Participants then took part in a signing ceremony and commemorative group photograph before concluding the event. Attendees pledged to continue international cooperation and collective responsibility in pursuit of a future of human co-prosperity, organizers said. The Joint Declaration of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 is presented during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul on June 12, 2026. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo 2026.06.12. Full Text of the Joint Declaration of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity (GAFH) 2026 Joint Declaration Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity (GAFH) 2026 We, the participants of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity (GAFH 2026), hereby expand the spirit of “Human Co-Prosperity” proclaimed in the 2025 Declaration of the Spirit of the AI Transformation Era to the international level, recognizing that the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is exerting a profound influence on the future of humanity and the international order. AI is a powerful tool capable of addressing humanity’s shared challenges, including the climate crisis, pandemics, educational inequality, poverty, and conflict. However, without proper control and accountability, it also poses risks that may threaten human dignity, freedom, democracy, and international peace. Therefore, we declare the following: Article 1. Spirit of the Era – Human Co-Prosperity The global direction of the AI era must be founded not on the interests of specific groups, but on the shared prosperity of all humankind. Technological advancement should proceed according to the principles of cooperation and responsibility, rather than competition and domination. Article 2. Human-Centered Values and Universal Principles AI must respect human dignity and fundamental rights and be developed and utilized under meaningful human oversight. The values of freedom, peace, equality, and respect for life must be embedded throughout the entire AI lifecycle. Article 3. Peace and International Security AI must serve as a tool for peace and cooperation, not for conflict or weaponization, and must never be used in ways that undermine international peace and security. Article 4. Fairness and Accountability We shall minimize inequality and discrimination arising from AI and strengthen international safety standards, transparency, and accountability frameworks for high-risk AI systems. Article 5. Global Governance To address the transnational impact of AI, we affirm that inclusive and responsible global governance is essential, involving international organizations, governments, businesses, academia, and civil society. The safety and accountability of AI are shared responsibilities of all humankind. Article 6. Contribution to Sustainable Development We will actively utilize AI to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), respond to climate change, prevent pandemics, advance education, eradicate poverty, and build peace. We reaffirm that AI is not a force to replace humanity, but a collaborative partner that expands human capability and responsibility. We declare that this agreement of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 will become an important milestone in the development of international AI governance, and we pledge to continue our shared responsibility and solidarity for the future of human co-prosperity. June 12, 2026 Participants of the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity (GAFH 2026)

title: [GAFH 2026] Global Experts: “AI Must Serve Human Co-Prosperity, Not Technological Hegemony”
partialText: [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] The Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) is being held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. Held under the theme, “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” the forum serves as an international platform for discussing how to harmonize advances in artificial intelligence with human-centered values. Hosted by Cheonji Ilbo (CEO Lee Sang-myeon), the event brought together approximately 300 experts and stakeholders from Korea and abroad. As AI continues to exert a growing influence across society, participants engaged in in-depth discussions on the importance of trustworthiness, ethics, and international cooperation in AI development and governance. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Yu Youngsun] As artificial intelligence (AI) emerges as one of the most powerful technologies in human history, the world stands at a critical turning point. While AI is opening new possibilities in healthcare, education, and industrial innovation, it is also creating unprecedented risks, including misinformation, deepfakes, surveillance, algorithmic bias, and autonomous weapons. Amid intensifying AI competition led by the United States and China, experts from around the world agreed that the most important issue is no longer the technology itself, but the direction in which it is developed and applied. They emphasized that AI should serve as a tool for the peace and prosperity of humanity rather than the interests of specific nations or corporations, and that the international community must establish shared principles and accountability mechanisms to achieve this goal. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] Lee Sang-myeon, CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, delivers the opening remarks at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. Held under the theme “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” the forum was organized as an international platform for discussions on harmonizing advances in artificial intelligence with human-centered values. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. To address these challenges, Cheonji Ilbo hosted the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) on June 12 at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Seoul. The forum attracted approximately 300 participants from politics, academia, media, industry, and civil society, reflecting growing public interest in the future of AI. Held under the theme “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” the event brought together leading AI experts, scholars, and industry representatives from around the world to discuss AI governance, human-centered values, responsible innovation, and strategies for building a trustworthy AI ecosystem. Participants highlighted the concept of “Human Co-Prosperity” as a guiding principle for the AI era, arguing that AI development should move beyond geopolitical competition and contribute to the shared advancement of all humanity. The forum concluded with the adoption of the Global Declaration on AI for Human Co-Prosperity, which encapsulated the key discussions and recommendations from the event. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] Lee Sang-myeon, CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, poses for a commemorative photograph with panelists during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026), held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. Held under the theme “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” the forum was organized as an international platform for discussions on harmonizing advances in artificial intelligence with human-centered values and promoting a shared vision for humanity's future. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. “In the AI Era, Values Matter More Than Technology” In his opening remarks, Lee Sang-myeon, Chairman of the Organizing Committee and CEO of Cheonji Ilbo, stressed that values—not technology—will determine the future of AI. “We are living in a time of profound transformation in which artificial intelligence is reshaping not only industries and economies but the very course of human civilization,” Lee said. “AI offers unprecedented opportunities to address longstanding challenges in healthcare, education, and social welfare. At the same time, however, it also accelerates risks such as misinformation, human alienation, surveillance, control, and militarization.” He emphasized that AI must be developed in a way that protects universal values such as human dignity and freedom while contributing to global peace, coexistence, and shared prosperity beyond national, cultural, and ideological boundaries. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] The Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 is being held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. During Session 1, panelist Andy Vermaut delivers a presentation titled “Global AI Governance: Building a Collaborative Framework for Human Co-Prosperity.” The session focuses on the importance of international cooperation and governance mechanisms to ensure that artificial intelligence contributes to the shared prosperity of humanity. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. “AI Knows No Borders”: The Need for Global Governance The first session focused on international cooperation and the establishment of global AI governance frameworks. Andy Vermaut, President of the World Council for Public Diplomacy and Community Dialogue (WCPDCC), emphasized the borderless nature of AI. “AI knows no borders. Therefore, our responsibility cannot stop at national borders,” he said. Vermaut noted that AI systems are often developed in one country, trained on data from multiple countries, and deployed worldwide, while legal and regulatory systems remain largely national in scope. As AI-related risks—including deepfakes, misinformation, automated fraud, and algorithmic bias—continue to grow, he argued that the international community must establish common standards and accountability frameworks. “Global AI governance is not about control by any particular nation,” he said. “It is about creating shared norms for transparency, accountability, and safety.” He called for an inclusive governance model involving both developed and developing countries, as well as large and small nations alike. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] The Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 is taking place at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12.During Session 1, Joo Young-sup, Distinguished Professor at the Graduate School of Engineering Practice at Seoul National University, delivers a presentation on “Global AI Governance: Building a Collaborative Framework for Human Co-Prosperity.” His presentation explores strategies for international cooperation and governance frameworks aimed at ensuring that AI contributes to sustainable development and shared prosperity for humanity. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. Professor Joo Young-sup, Distinguished Professor at Seoul National University's Graduate School of Engineering Practice, presented Korea’s strategic direction in the age of AI transformation. “AI is not an end in itself,” he said. “It is a means to achieve human happiness and sustainable development.” He argued that Korea should move beyond its traditional role as a fast follower and become a global leader in advancing the vision of human co-prosperity. Professor Joo identified the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and ESG principles as key tools for building AI governance in the future. “Technology ultimately moves toward the purposes that humanity chooses,” he noted. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Dr. Park Jeong-jin, a cultural anthropologist (center), and Lalit Agarwal, Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation in India (right), respond to questions following their presentations at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. The two speakers presented on the theme of embedding ethics and peace into artificial intelligence, emphasizing the importance of human-centered values, social responsibility, and the role of AI in promoting peace and coexistence. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. “Peace and Ethics Must Be Built into Algorithms” The second session explored human-centered values, peace, and ethics in the AI era. Cultural anthropologist Dr. Park Jeong-jin warned that humanity risks moving from being “a species that asks questions” to “a species that merely receives recommendations.” He described the AI revolution as a process of automating human thought and argued that the central challenge of the AI era is ensuring that humans are not reduced to machines. Dr. Park also warned that future warfare could increasingly rely on AI-powered autonomous weapons and algorithm-driven conflict. “Rather than restoring peace after war, we must design peace and ethics into algorithms from the beginning,” he said. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Dr. Park Jeong-jin (center), a cultural anthropologist, and Lalit Agarwal (right), Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation in India, answer questions following their presentations at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. The speakers delivered presentations on the theme of embedding ethics and peace into artificial intelligence, highlighting the importance of ensuring that AI development aligns with human values and contributes to a more peaceful and inclusive society. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. Lalit Agarwal, Vice Chancellor of the MERI Foundation, identified the “Empathy Divide” as a fundamental source of social conflict. “While we are more digitally connected than ever, we are becoming increasingly divided socially,” he said. Agarwal advocated the development of AI-powered peace education systems and introduced TARP, a conflict-prediction framework designed to help societies anticipate and mitigate tensions. “Peace is not accidental—it is a social capability that can be learned,” he explained. “The Future of AI Depends on Trust” The third session focused on trustworthy AI design and industrialization strategies. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Choi Eun-soo, CEO of Intellivix, delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. His presentation focuses on the importance of building trustworthy AI systems and explores strategies for translating AI innovation into practical industrial applications while ensuring transparency, accountability, and safety. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. Choi Eun-soo, CEO of Intellivix, argued that future competitiveness in the AI industry will depend not on performance alone but on trust. “AI is no longer merely a tool for analysis,” he said. “It is becoming a technology that acts in the real world.” He warned that failures in AI systems used in autonomous vehicles or industrial facilities could result in significant social harm. Choi introduced the T.R.U.S.T. Framework, which incorporates explainability, traceability, human oversight, double verification, and accountability. “The future will belong not to the most autonomous AI, but to the most controllable AI,” he stated. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Nam Seung-woo] Li Haonan, CEO of Simeng Technology, delivers a presentation on “Trustworthy AI Design and Industrialization” at the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026, held at the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on June 12. During his presentation, Li discusses the importance of trust, transparency, and accountability in AI development, emphasizing the role of reliable AI systems in driving sustainable industrial innovation and large-scale adoption. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. Li Haonan, CEO of Simeng AI, emphasized that the future of AI will be determined not by technical features but by practical applications in industry. “The key question is not what AI can do, but what kind of transformation it can create,” he said. “Without trust, neither large-scale deployment nor industrialization is possible.” He added that transparency, safety, and accountability must serve as the minimum common standards for the global AI era. “AI Is Humanity’s Partner”: Global Declaration Adopted The forum concluded with the presentation and adoption of the Global Declaration on AI for Human Co-Prosperity. [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] The Global Declaration on AI for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 is presented during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026), held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. The declaration outlines shared principles for ensuring that artificial intelligence advances the common good of humanity, emphasizing human dignity, trust, accountability, international cooperation, and the responsible development and use of AI technologies. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026. The declaration states that AI development should pursue the shared prosperity of humanity rather than the interests of any particular nation, corporation, or group. It further calls for universal values—including human dignity, freedom, peace, equality, and respect for life—to be embedded throughout the entire AI lifecycle. The declaration also emphasizes that AI should become a tool for peace and cooperation rather than conflict and militarization. Through a formal signing ceremony, participants affirmed that AI safety and accountability are shared responsibilities requiring international solidarity and cooperation. The forum was widely recognized for presenting a new vision for the AI era—one that moves beyond technological competition and focuses on human co-prosperity and trustworthy AI. The Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026) is being held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. Held under the theme “Trustworthy AI for Human Co-Prosperity,” the forum serves as an international platform for dialogue on harmonizing advances in artificial intelligence with human-centered values. The event brings together experts, academics, industry leaders, and policymakers to discuss AI governance, ethics, trust, and strategies for ensuring that AI contributes to the shared prosperity of humanity. Participants concluded with a shared message: “AI is not a replacement for humanity. It is a partner that expands human capabilities and responsibilities. More than ever, we need common principles and international cooperation to build a better future for all.” [Cheonji Ilbo=Reporter Park Jun-seong] Participants pose for a commemorative photograph after signing the Global Declaration on AI for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 during the Global AI Forum for Human Co-Prosperity 2026 (GAFH 2026), held at the International Conference Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the afternoon of June 12. The declaration reflects a shared commitment to promoting trustworthy, responsible, and human-centered artificial intelligence, while strengthening international cooperation for the common prosperity of humanity. ⓒ Cheonji Ilbo, June 12, 2026.
